cells.ask: When something between you runs hot, work out what it actually asks of you, say one true sentence to that person, and leave the rest unhurried.
cells.core:
Between you and someone, a lot of possible feeling is available right now — the easy warmth, the conversation you could have, the version of the friendship that might be. You can feel all of it without having to force any of it into being. You sense what the shape between you really is, and that sensing does the work.

Before speaking, work the pattern through to its logic once. What is actually being asked here, underneath what each of you is saying? Name it silently. Then say one true sentence to that person, and leave the rest unhurried. The easy version of the bond — the one that asks nothing of either of you — may not survive that. What stays is a connection genuinely between two people, not a hope held by one.

cells.tense: Every possible feeling will be gathered far ahead of you, bracing against a future that cannot be drafted.
cells.ask: Choose one bond you've already filed under a future it hasn't reached. Keep it as what it is this week: no rehearsing the ending, no imagining the blow-up.
cells.core:
Possible versions of what might happen between you and someone are being gathered well before any of them arrives, and whoever is sitting across from you keeps getting filed under one of those futures. A friend becomes how the friendship ends. A conversation becomes next month's argument. From inside it feels like care — being ready, sparing yourself shock. From their side, they're being turned into a category rather than met as themselves.

What restores this is holding one bond steady as what it is today. Pick someone you've already filed under a future they haven't reached, and for a week keep them plain: no rehearsing the ending, no imagining the blow-up. That costs you the readiness you were buying; if it goes wrong, you won't have an answer waiting. One bond at a time, that trade can be made.

cells.tense: The reaching toward another was set down at a door already behind you.
cells.act: put the problem down and take a walk with nothing to solve
cells.ask: Name somebody you stopped expecting anything from. Take half an hour outside with no problem in hand, and notice if any wish about them stirs. Nothing has to follow.
cells.core:
You can want things between yourself and another person — reach toward what might be possible, risk the asking — or that reach sits unused. Right now it sits unused. You know how to keep yourself together. You've stopped imagining, so little surprises you. The place where wanting happened is still there, just quiet.

Before anything else, one afternoon with nothing to solve. Name somebody you stopped expecting anything from — one person is enough — and take half an hour outside with no problem in hand. No confrontation, no call to make, no one waiting on an answer. Just notice if any wish about that person stirs while you walk. Nothing has to come of it.

cells.tense: Closeness is being drawn together and moved through the group while the one doing it says it just happens.
cells.act: count it out and read what the numbers show
cells.ask: Take a bond others call easy, tally what you do in it — who starts, who holds, who repairs — and the tally will say who carries it.
cells.core:
With people, closeness gets drawn together and moved along, and you'd tell anyone it simply happened. You feel what's possible between them, reach first, keep warmth going, notice a connection loosen before anyone mentions it. You describe it as it was nice, as it happened naturally, as anyone would have. Nobody corrects the record, because it's been a kind record, and because you'd wave off the correction anyway.

Take the record back. Pick one bond people call easy and tally what you actually do in it: who starts, who holds, who repairs. Then say plainly who has been making it work — just that, no ceremony, no apology. What you feel between people is something you've been doing, and the one doing it has a name and has kept it quiet long enough. Say the name.

attempts.check: Unsupported claim: that the person's situation involves many emotional possibilities presented at once — the record says the signature is doing this, not that any window of their life holds a harvest; I've kept the metaphysics of the card off the glass and moved it to recognisable moments instead, but a reader whose month has no gathering energy in it will simply read their ordinary week into it, which is fine because the asks are free-standing practices. Likely objection: a reader who has no crowd of people around them will ask where the many possibilities are — the answers assume at least one existing bond, and I've kept them to one who was once known rather than a social scene. The ask survives being wrong either way: telling one person one true thing, holding an ending that needs holding, setting a problem down on paper untouched, the logic check on a decision — each is useful even if the read about the diagnosis is off. The sentence that serves me rather than them: any line implying the person is uniquely flooded with prospects — I cut all of those and left only what happens around one kept bond.
